Another enriching component of the program was the reading and reflection of books by authors such as James Clear, Brianna Wiest, and Darius Foroux. These works encouraged self-reflection, continuous improvement, and the mindset of a lifelong learner.

Perhaps the most profound lesson was understanding the transition from trainer to mentor.

Annete ma'am is an exceptional coach, mentor, and educator.  She has a unique ability to bring out the best in her learners and inspire them to strive for excellence.

I am deeply grateful to Empower English Academy and Annete ma'am for this incredible learning journey. The program has enriched me both professionally and personally, and I would highly recommend it to anyone seeking to become a skilled trainer, communicator, leader, and lifelong learner.

Most people look at their spoken English and say, “I’m weak in English.”
But here’s the truth: you’re not weak in English - you’re just not used to using it out loud.
Think about it: you understand English every day. You watch videos, read messages, scroll through social media, and listen to songs - all in English.
Yet when it’s time to speak, the mind suddenly switches off.
That’s not because the language is too hard.
It’s because your brain has never been trained to produce it, only to receive it.
Speaking English is like using a muscle.
If you never lift weights, your arms will feel weak.
If you never speak English, your mouth will feel clumsy.
But the moment you start practicing aloud, everything begins to change.
You don’t need to be perfect.
You just need to be active.
Start with something small: say three simple English sentences out loud every day.
“I am ready for the day.”
“I want to speak better.”
“I trust myself.”
Repeat them.
Feel them.
Own them.
That’s how the real journey begins - not with a big goal, but with a tiny habit.
You’re not bad at English.
You’re just one step away from becoming fluent.
